chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddiq ibn Sadah, from Ammar ibn Musa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about a man who marries his female slave to his male slave, and then wishes to separate them, so the male slave runs away. What should he do? He said: 'He says to her,

key_terms.لَمْ يَقَعْ طَلاَقُهُ: his divorce did not take effect
key_terms.يُجَامِعُهَا: he has sexual intercourse with her

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on separating a married slave couple and the validity of their divorce?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* elucidates the specific mechanics of *Tamyiz* (separation) within the master's right of option over slave marriages, distinguishing between consummated and unconsummated unions. It highlights the Shia juristic view that the master's declaration effectively dissolves the bond, triggering a five-day waiting period (*Iddah*) for consummated cases to ensure lineage clarity, while unconsummated cases require no waiting period. The text further clarifies the autonomy of the slave's divorce power, noting that it is contingent upon the master's permission, reflecting the hierarchical yet legally structured nature of *Milk al-Yamin* relationships.
